findings.claim: The 'Non-negotiable verification constraint' block in §5 step 3 instructs 023C to 'use the --source-path-prefix and --predicate-type filters' in the gh attestation verify invocation. --source-path-prefix is not a recognised flag in gh attestation verify; it does not exist in the gh CLI's attestation verify subcommand. The correct flag for verifying the signing workflow's identity (which maps to the job_workflow_ref OIDC claim in the Sigstore certificate SAN) is --signer-workflow. An executor following the 'MUST use' directive literally will encounter an unknown-flag error; if they then remove the unrecognised flag and proceed with only --predicate-type, the invocation verifies SLSA provenance type but does not bind to the specific SCP reusable workflow path — reopening the rogue-workflow forgery path that MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 closed at the plan-doc level.
findings.evidence: Plan-doc §5 step 3, Non-negotiable verification constraint block (added in fix-round-2): 'The 023C gh attestation verify invocation MUST use the --source-path-prefix and --predicate-type filters to bind the attestation to the SCP reusable workflow at the expected SHA; an attestation produced by any other workflow (custom or third-party) MUST be rejected with verification_failure: untrusted_workflow_source.' gh attestation verify recognised flags include: --bundle, --cert-identity, --cert-identity-regexp, --cert-oidc-issuer, --cert-oidc-issuer-url, --digest-alg, --format, --json-results, --no-public-good, --owner, --predicate-type, --repo, --signer-repo, --signer-workflow. --predicate-type is a real flag filtering by SLSA predicate type (e.g. https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1). --source-path-prefix is not present; it appears to conflate nomenclature from OCI/cosign tooling or an earlier draft. --signer-workflow is the real gh attestation verify flag that checks the workflow file path embedded in the Sigstore certificate SAN (format: owner/repo/.github/workflows/name.yml@ref), which is the direct representation of the job_workflow_ref OIDC claim. The security requirement itself is correctly stated in the preceding sentence ('the aggregator MUST verify the job_workflow_ref OIDC claim'), so the intent is unambiguous; the implementation guidance sub-clause contains the incorrect flag name.
findings.impact: Primary risk: a 023C Codex executor who treats the 'MUST use' clause as the definitive implementation specification attempts 'gh attestation verify --source-path-prefix <path> --predicate-type <type>'; the CLI rejects --source-path-prefix as unknown; the executor removes the flag to make the invocation succeed; the result is SLSA provenance type filtering only, without workflow-path binding. Any workflow in an opted-in adopter's repo whose artifact carries a SLSA provenance attestation would then pass the aggregator's verification — the rogue-adopter-workflow forgery vector that MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 closed at the plan-doc level is re-opened at the implementation level. Secondary mitigation: the security requirement ('MUST verify the job_workflow_ref OIDC claim') is clearly stated and would be checked by 023C's R1 safety reviewer. The net risk is implementation churn and potential need for a 023C fix-round, rather than a shipped bypass.
findings.mitigation: In §5 step 3 Non-negotiable verification constraint block, replace '--source-path-prefix' with '--signer-workflow' (the real gh attestation verify flag for binding to a specific signing workflow path). Updated sentence: 'The 023C gh attestation verify invocation MUST use the --signer-workflow and --predicate-type filters to bind the attestation to the SCP reusable workflow at the expected SHA; an attestation produced by any other workflow (custom or third-party) MUST be rejected with verification_failure: untrusted_workflow_source.' Add a parenthetical note after the flag names: '(flag names should be verified against the gh CLI version pinned in .github/workflows/scorecard-aggregator.yml at 023C implementation time).' Inline-fix; no descope.

The R2 safety reviewer's MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 mitigation recommendation called for updating 'both §9 of the plan-doc AND docs/DECISIONS.md header note' with the mandatory claim verification requirement. Fix-round-2 added the constraint to §5 step 3 only (binding it to D-042 by name there), but did not update DECISIONS.md or §9. A 023C Codex executor scanning DECISIONS.md to understand D-042's scope before reading the full plan-doc would find: 'Aggregator pipeline trust model — GitHub Actions Artifact Attestation for adopter emits + SCP-side Ed25519 key registry' — with no explicit flag that D-042 MUST implement job_workflow_ref claim verification as a non-negotiable requirement.

No job_workflow_ref or claim verification language present. Ratifies invariants 6–8 in workflow form.' No job_workflow_ref language. Plan-doc §5 step 3 Non-negotiable constraint block: 'the aggregator MUST verify the job_workflow_ref OIDC claim... (per D-042 + closes 023A R2 MAJ-SAFE-R2-001)' — constraint IS bound to D-042 here. FIX-ROUND-2.md inline-fix summary lists 6 edits (§1, §5 Job1 permissions, §5 step3, §8, §10 Q1, DISPATCH-NOTE.md) with no DECISIONS.md update. R2 safety review json MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 mitigation: 'Add a non-negotiable content constraint to the D-042 reservation block in both §9 of the plan-doc and docs/DECISIONS.md header note.'
findings.impact: A 023C Codex executor who reads DECISIONS.md for D-042's scope would not encounter the job_workflow_ref requirement in that index. Compounded with MIN-SAFE-R3-001 (incorrect flag name in §5), a mechanically compliant executor could file D-042 with OIDC signature verification that omits workflow-path binding. The §5 constraint is the definitive specification and the DISPATCH-NOTE for 023C would reference the plan-doc; 023C's R1 safety review would catch an incorrect implementation. Net effect is risk of implementation churn rather than a shipped bypass, but the partial implementation of the R2 mitigation leaves a documentation gap across the two canonical entry points (DECISIONS.md and §9) where a 023C executor would look for D-042 scope.
findings.mitigation: Append to the DECISIONS.md D-042 reservation blockquote: 'Mandatory trust constraint (closes 023A R2 MAJ-SAFE-R2-001, per §5 step 3): the 023C aggregator MUST verify the job_workflow_ref OIDC claim in each artifact attestation against the SCP reusable workflow path AND SHA pin; OIDC JWKS signature verification alone is not sufficient.' Update §9 D-042 table row to include: '+ mandatory job_workflow_ref OIDC claim verification against SCP reusable workflow path + SHA pin (closes 023A R2 MAJ-SAFE-R2-001).' Inline-fix; no descope.

self_reported_concerns: MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 CLOSED: Plan-doc §5 step 3 Non-negotiable verification constraint block (added in fix-round-2, HEAD ac48843) is present and verified. It names the claim (job_workflow_ref), the verification target (SCP reusable workflow path AND SHA pin), the threat (any workflow in an opted-in adopter's repo could fabricate an emit and pass JWKS-only verification), and the rejection behavior (verification_failure: untrusted_workflow_source). The block is labeled 'Non-negotiable' and explicitly bound to D-042 by name ('per D-042 + closes 023A R2 MAJ-SAFE-R2-001'). A 023C Codex executor reading §5 step 3 cannot legitimately satisfy D-042 without implementing this constraint. Wording is unambiguous. Actionable for 023C. CLOSED — with one residual MIN-SAFE-R3-001 (implementation guidance names incorrect flag --source-path-prefix; the security requirement itself is correctly stated).

PERMISSION CHANGE VERIFIED — NO WEAKENING: id-token:write → attestations:read in §5 Job 1 aggregate job is a security improvement. id-token:write is the GitHub Actions permission that allows a job to REQUEST a fresh OIDC token from GitHub's identity provider — used when the job needs to prove its own identity to an external service (e.g. Sigstore/Fulcio during artifact signing). The aggregate job is VERIFYING others' attestations, not creating its own; it does not need to request an OIDC token. attestations:read is the correct permission for calling GitHub's Artifact Attestation API (read operations). Removing id-token:write reduces the aggregate job's privilege footprint and eliminates an unnecessary capability. Two-job permission scoping (read-only aggregate + write-scoped commit, commit fires only on aggregate success) is preserved and unchanged. VERIFIED CORRECT — no weakening of verification model.

BYPASS SURFACE INVENTORY R3 STATUS: (1) Tampered emit — rogue adopter workflow forgery: job_workflow_ref constraint in §5 step 3 closes this path at the plan-doc level; bound to D-042; MIN-SAFE-R3-001 notes incorrect implementation guidance flag but does not reopen the bypass at plan-doc level; 023C R1 will verify implementation. (2) Tampered index — SCP-side Ed25519 key registry + CODEOWNERS on output/scorecards/** + two-job permission scoping unchanged; bus-factor-1 acknowledged in invariant 7 and §4 threat model exclusion; no new surface from R2 fixes. (3) MCP enumeration — aggregated-only output, no raw waiver content, rate limits per WP-SCP-021, read-only posture; invariant 5 unchanged; src/** CODEOWNERS coverage (MAJ-SAFE-003 R1 closure) protects the MCP server source. (4) Opt-in registry tamper — docs/scorecards/** @jrnb2024 CODEOWNERS (MIN-SAFE-005 R1 closure) unchanged; PR review required for any adopter row change. (5) Aggregator workflow tamper — .github/** @jrnb2024 CODEOWNERS unchanged; id-token:write removed reduces privilege footprint; no new surface. (6) TOCTOU — artifact attestation binding (artifact digest in Sigstore certificate) mitigates mid-flight substitution; the race between run-selection and artifact-download produces at most a different legitimately-signed emit, not a forgery. (7) Symlink — not applicable; GitHub artifact API downloads are network-based REST operations. (8) Concurrent aggregator runs — concurrent cron + manual-trigger runs each produce separate PRs; no shared state race toward the index file; operator handles merge sequencing.

TF-FORWARDS ACCURACY VERIFIED: TF-023A-001 (low priority: clarify R-023-01 k-anonymity framing when WP-SCP-024 cascade slice begins) — accurately reflects the open item. nit-SAFE-R2-001 (TF timing misaligned to WP-SCP-024 vs 023D kickoff) was classified NO ACTION in R2; TF remains as filed. No safety bypass surface. TF-023A-002 (medium priority: cross-repo notification to ACC/CT/mapp-estate-regression at 023B kickoff) — accurately reflects the cross-repo coordination residual; completeness/coordination concern, not a safety surface. FIX-ROUND-2.md correctly states no new TF candidates were filed in R2. Both TFs carry forward accurately.

PRE-EXISTING AMBIGUITY — NOT A NEW FINDING: §5 step 3 contains a latent textual ambiguity inherited from R1: the opening paragraph describes the key registry model with 'each emit carries its signing key_id' (implying Ed25519 signing of adopter emits), while the 'Signing mechanism' sub-block explicitly states 'No private signing key is ever distributed to adopter runners' and describes OIDC attestation for adopter emits. At R3 I verified: (a) the 'Signing mechanism' block is unambiguous that adopter emits use OIDC, not Ed25519; (b) the key registry (Ed25519, from docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub) applies to the SCP-side aggregator-emitted central index only; (c) this ambiguity predates R2 and was acknowledged implicitly in the R2 self_reported_concerns ('for adopter emits, the shift to OIDC attestation removes the SCP key rotation cliff entirely for that signing path'). The ambiguity could cause documentation confusion for a 023C executor but the OIDC path is the clearly governing mechanism for adopter emits. Classifying as pre-existing documentation clarity residual, not a new R3 safety finding. The Non-negotiable constraint block reinforces the OIDC path and makes the signing mechanism unambiguous for the security-critical verification step.
summary: All R2 safety findings verified closed at HEAD ac48843 (fix-round-2). MAJ-SAFE-R2-001 is closed: §5 step 3 now contains a 'Non-negotiable verification constraint' block that explicitly requires the aggregator to verify the job_workflow_ref OIDC claim against the expected SCP reusable workflow path AND SHA pin, explains the threat (rogue-adopter workflow forgery), names the rejection code (verification_failure: untrusted_workflow_source), and binds the requirement to D-042 by name — unambiguous and actionable for 023C. The id-token:write → attestations:read permission change is a security improvement: id-token:write would grant the aggregate job the ability to request a new OIDC token for its own identity (unnecessary); attestations:read is the correct permission for reading and verifying existing artifact attestations via gh attestation verify against GitHub's Artifact Attestation API. Bypass surface inventory rerun: all five surfaces unchanged or hardened — the job_workflow_ref constraint closes the rogue-adopter-workflow forgery path; no new surface introduced by R2 fixes. Two new MIN findings: MIN-SAFE-R3-001 (the Non-negotiable constraint block names --source-path-prefix as a required gh attestation verify filter, but that flag does not exist in the gh CLI; the correct workflow-identity flag is --signer-workflow; an executor who attempts the non-existent flag and removes it to make the command succeed could end up without workflow-path binding) and MIN-SAFE-R3-002 (the DECISIONS.md D-042 reservation note and §9 table do not name the job_workflow_ref constraint, partially implementing the R2 mitigation recommendation; a 023C Codex executor reading only DECISIONS.md would not see this mandatory requirement). TF-023A-001 and TF-023A-002 accurately reflect remaining open items; no new TFs were filed in R2. No new CRIT or MAJ findings. Plan-doc is merge-ready pending two MIN inline fixes.
